notes.meaning: God has promised to be a loving Father and live among his people. Because of these wonderful promises, believers should turn away from everything that defiles either the body or the inner thoughts. Growing in holiness means letting God shape our whole lives out of deep reverence for him.

differ.view: Christians should not settle for merely avoiding bad habits, but should press on toward entire holiness in love and conduct during this life.
Believers are commanded to aim for complete holiness, but no one reaches sinless perfection until they are with Christ in heaven.

notes.meaning: Paul asks the Corinthians to make room for him and his coworkers in their hearts. He reminds them that he has never treated anyone unfairly, taught false ideas to lead anyone astray, or taken money from them by cheating. He lived with pure motives so they could trust him fully.

Paul makes clear that he is not defending himself just to point fingers or blame the Corinthians. He loves them so much that they share a permanent place in his heart. His bond with them is so strong that he would gladly live or die together with them.

Paul feels able to speak with complete honesty because he has such great pride in the church at Corinth. Hearing about their response gave him immense comfort. Even though he was facing heavy troubles on his travels, his joy completely overflowed.

When Paul arrived in the region of Macedonia, he found no rest for his weary body. Enemies opposed him fiercely on the outside, and anxious worries weighed on his mind from the inside. He was especially troubled because he had not yet heard how the Corinthians had received his instruction.

God specializes in bringing encouragement to those who feel low, anxious, and worn down. He answered Paul's distress by sending his fellow worker Titus with good news. God often uses Christian friends to carry his comfort to our aching hearts.

Paul was cheered not only by seeing Titus again, but by hearing how warmly the Corinthians had treated him. Titus shared that they missed Paul, grieved over the sins in their church, and showed great devotion to him. This wonderful report made Paul's remaining sorrow melt into deep joy.

Paul had written a very firm letter to correct disorders in the church, and for a short time his tender heart felt bad for causing them distress. Now he no longer regrets sending it, because he sees that the pain lasted only a short time. Necessary correction hurts at first, but it brings healthy healing.

Paul rejoices now, not because they felt emotional pain, but because their pain led them to repentance. Repentance means a real change of mind and direction toward God. Because their grief was the kind God intended, Paul's hard words ended up helping them rather than doing any harm.

Godly sorrow happens when a person realizes they have sinned against God, and it leads them to a genuine change of life that ends in salvation. No one ever looks back and regrets that kind of sorrow. In contrast, worldly sorrow only grieves over getting caught or losing status, and that selfish despair leads to spiritual ruin and death.

Paul points out how godly sorrow changed the church's behavior. Instead of ignoring sin, they showed great eagerness to make things right, defended their commitment to holiness, and felt anger toward the evil deed. Their quick and sincere discipline showed that they were now clean and free from guilt in the matter.

Paul explains that his main reason for writing was not simply to punish the wrongdoer or comfort the injured person. He wrote so the whole church could see before God how much they truly cared about walking in obedience. Church discipline aims to guard the health and purity of the whole church family.

Seeing the church restored and at peace gave Paul great comfort. His happiness rose even higher when he saw how joyfully Titus returned. Titus felt deeply refreshed in spirit because all the believers in Corinth had received him so well.

Paul had previously told Titus that the Corinthians were good people at heart who would do the right thing. He was not put to shame, because their respectful actions proved his boast was accurate. Just as Paul had always spoken God's truth to them, his praise of them to Titus was proven true.

Titus now feels an even deeper affection for the Corinthians as he remembers their willingness to listen and obey. They had welcomed him with fear and trembling, which means with deep humility and serious concern not to dishonor God's message. Sincere obedience draws Christian leaders and their people closer together.

Paul wraps up this part of his letter by rejoicing that he can have total confidence in the Corinthians. Their quick repentance and obedience showed that their faith was genuine and solid. Having this trust restored brought him great peace and courage.
